content:
Short answer: A Hong Kong visit visa is needed if your passport is not on Hong Kong's visa-free list, or if you want to stay longer than your visa-free period. You apply to the Hong Kong Immigration Department (ImmD) with form ID 1003A, a passport copy, a photo, proof of money and your travel plans. You can apply online, by post or through a Chinese embassy where you live. Processing normally takes about four weeks, and approved visitors receive an e-Visa.

Sponsor formID 1003B (optional but helpful)

Normal processing timeAbout 4 weeks once the file is complete

What is a Hong Kong visit visa?

A Hong Kong visit visa is permission to enter Hong Kong for a short stay. It covers tourism, visiting family or friends, attending business meetings and passing through on the way somewhere else. It does not let you work, study or start a business.

Hong Kong runs its own immigration system, separate from mainland China. That surprises many first-time travellers. A China visa does not let you into Hong Kong, and a Hong Kong visit visa does not let you into the mainland. If your trip includes both, plan two separate applications.

The Hong Kong visit visa is issued by the Immigration Department in Hong Kong itself. Chinese embassies and consulates abroad only collect applications and pass them on. That is why decisions can take longer than people expect: your file usually travels to Hong Kong and back.

Do you need a Hong Kong visit visa?

Many nationalities can visit Hong Kong without a visa. Depending on your passport, the visa-free stay is anywhere from 7 to 180 days. British citizens, for example, can usually stay up to 180 days without a visa. You need a Hong Kong visit visa if:

  • your nationality is not on ImmD's visa-free list
  • you want to stay longer than your visa-free period allows
  • you have been refused entry before and want certainty before you fly
  • you hold a travel document that is not accepted for visa-free entry

Check your nationality on the ImmD "Visa Requirements for Visitors" page before you start. Rules change, so check again shortly before you travel. Indian nationals, for instance, have their own pre-arrival registration route and apply directly to ImmD rather than through a Chinese embassy.

How do you apply for a Hong Kong visit visa, step by step?

The Hong Kong visit visa process is simple once you know the order. Follow these eight steps.

  1. Check you need a visa. Look up your passport on the ImmD visa requirements list. If you can enter visa-free for the length of your trip, you do not need to apply.
  2. Download form ID 1003A. It is free on the ImmD website. Fill it in with your details exactly as printed in your passport, including middle names.
  3. Find a sponsor if you can. A Hong Kong company, or a Hong Kong resident aged 18 or over who knows you, can fill in form ID 1003B. A sponsor is optional, but it helps ImmD verify your visit.
  4. Collect your documents. Use the checklist in the next section. Make clear copies and keep originals safe.
  5. Choose how to submit. Apply online through GovHK, post the forms to ImmD Headquarters in Tseung Kwan O (yourself or through your sponsor), or hand them in at the Chinese embassy or consulate where you live.
  6. Pay the fee. The current amount is on the ImmD fee table. Online you can pay by card. By post you need a cashier order or bank draft, never cash.
  7. Wait for the decision. ImmD normally needs about four weeks after it receives every document. It will not start on an incomplete file.
  8. Save your e-Visa. On arrival, show your passport and the e-Visa QR code on your phone or a printed A4 copy at the immigration counter.

What documents do you need for a Hong Kong visit visa?

A complete file is the biggest factor you control. For a Hong Kong visit visa, ImmD asks for:

  • Form ID 1003A, completed and signed, with a recent passport photo attached
  • A copy of your passport's personal details page, showing issue and expiry dates
  • Proof of money, such as three to six months of bank statements, tax records or a salary slip
  • Proof of employment if you have a job, such as a letter from your employer
  • Your travel plans, including a flight itinerary and accommodation
  • Proof of your purpose: a tour itinerary for holidays, an invitation letter for business, or proof of your relationship with the person you are visiting
  • Sponsor documents if you have a sponsor: form ID 1003B plus a Business Registration Certificate for a company, or a Hong Kong ID card copy for an individual

If your sponsor is a non-permanent Hong Kong resident, they also send a copy of their travel document with their latest arrival stamp or extension label. Our guide to visa cover letters shows how to explain your trip in a short letter, and the rules for photos are in digital photos for visa applications.

Can someone in Hong Kong sponsor your visit visa?

Yes. A sponsor can make your Hong Kong visit visa application easier to verify, especially for family or business visits. There are two kinds of sponsor:

  • A company in Hong Kong. It fills in form ID 1003B and adds a copy of its Business Registration Certificate.
  • An individual who is at least 18, lives in Hong Kong as a genuine resident and knows you personally. They fill in form ID 1003B and add a copy of their Hong Kong identity card.

Sponsors can also post the complete application to ImmD for you. This is often faster than going through an embassy, because the papers reach Hong Kong directly.

How much does a Hong Kong visit visa cost?

The fee is set by ImmD and published in its fee table. It is charged per application and is not refunded if the visa is refused. When you apply through a Chinese embassy or consulate, they may add their own handling charge. If you post your application, pay with a cashier order or bank draft made out as ImmD instructs. Never send cash.

Budget for these extra costs too:

  • passport photos that meet the rules
  • courier or registered post
  • translation of documents that are not in English or Chinese
  • travel insurance, which ImmD does not require but which is wise for any trip

How long does a Hong Kong visit visa take?

ImmD says it normally needs about four weeks after it receives all the required documents. If it asks for something extra, the clock effectively restarts when that document arrives. Applications through a Chinese embassy can take longer because of the extra handling.

We recommend applying at least six weeks before you travel. That leaves time to answer questions and still keep your flight dates. Avoid booking non-refundable flights until your Hong Kong visit visa is approved.

What does the Hong Kong e-Visa look like?

If your Hong Kong visit visa is approved, ImmD issues an e-Visa. It is an electronic document with your details and a QR code. You can:

  • keep it on your phone
  • print it on A4 paper
  • do both, which is the safest option

At the immigration counter you show your passport and the e-Visa, and the officer scans the QR code. Visas issued through Chinese missions or the Hong Kong offices in Beijing and Shanghai may instead come as a label stuck in your passport.

[IMG2]

What are the most common Hong Kong visit visa mistakes?

Most delays and refusals come from small, avoidable problems. Watch out for these:

  • Applying through the wrong channel. If you live outside Hong Kong, use the Chinese mission where you live, unless your nationality is told to apply directly to ImmD.
  • Sending cash by post. Postal fees must be a cashier order or bank draft.
  • Weak proof of money. One statement with a large recent deposit raises questions. Three to six months of normal activity reads much better.
  • No clear purpose. "Tourism" with no plan is harder to approve than a simple day-by-day itinerary.
  • Faxing only. You may fax forms first, but the visa is only issued once the originals arrive.
  • Names that do not match. Every form must match your passport exactly.

What can you do on a Hong Kong visit visa?

A Hong Kong visit visa lets you do what visitors normally do: sightseeing, visiting family, attending meetings and conferences, and transiting. You cannot:

  • take paid or unpaid work
  • start or join a business
  • enrol as a student
  • stay longer than the period stamped or shown on your e-Visa

If you want to work or study in Hong Kong, you need a different visa, usually sponsored by an employer or a school.

A real example: a family visit to Hong Kong

Imagine Amina, a teacher living in Nairobi, wants to visit her brother who works in Hong Kong. Her passport is not visa-free. She fills in form ID 1003A and attaches her photo. Her brother fills in form ID 1003B and adds a copy of his Hong Kong ID card and his latest arrival stamp.

Amina adds six months of bank statements, a letter from her school confirming her job and approved leave, a return flight reservation, and a copy of her brother's tenancy agreement as proof of where she will stay. She also adds a short cover letter explaining the visit. Her brother posts the whole file to ImmD. She hears back in just under four weeks and receives her e-Visa by email.

What made this work was simple: a clear purpose, strong proof of ties at home, and a sponsor who could be verified.

What happens after your Hong Kong visit visa is approved?

Once you have your e-Visa:

  1. Check every detail: name, passport number, dates and length of stay.
  2. Book or confirm your flights and accommodation.
  3. Carry printed copies of your bank statements and return ticket, in case the officer asks.
  4. Keep within your permitted stay. Overstaying can lead to a ban on future visits.

Hong Kong visit visa, visa-free entry or transit: which applies to you?

People often mix up the three ways of entering Hong Kong. This table shows the difference.

OptionWho it suitsDo you apply first?
Visa-free entryNationalities on ImmD's visa-free list, for stays within their allowed periodNo, you just show your passport
Hong Kong visit visaNationalities that need a visa, or anyone staying longer than their visa-free periodYes, to ImmD
TransitTravellers passing through to another destinationDepends on nationality; some need a transit visa

If you are only changing planes and staying airside, you usually do not need anything. If you leave the airport, the normal entry rules apply.

How can you make your Hong Kong visit visa application stronger?

ImmD looks for three things: a believable purpose, enough money, and reasons to go home. Here is how to show each one.

Show a clear purpose

Write a short day-by-day plan. For a family visit, explain who you are visiting and how you are related. For business, include an invitation letter on company letterhead that names you, the dates and the purpose of the meetings.

Show you can pay for the trip

Bank statements should cover three to six months and show regular income. A sudden large deposit just before you apply looks like borrowed money. If someone else is paying, include their letter and their statements.

Show you will return home

A letter from your employer confirming your job and approved leave is powerful. Property papers, a business registration, or a letter from your university also help. These show ImmD that your life is at home and your Hong Kong visit visa will be used as intended.

Can children apply for a Hong Kong visit visa?

Yes. Each child needs their own application, even if they travel on a parent's passport where that is allowed. A parent or guardian signs the form. Include the child's birth certificate to prove the relationship, and a consent letter if the child travels with only one parent or with another adult.

What if your Hong Kong visit visa is refused?

ImmD does not always give a detailed reason. Look at your file honestly: was the purpose clear, was the money convincing, and were the documents complete? You can reapply with a stronger file. Add the missing proof rather than resending the same papers. A short cover letter explaining what has changed helps.

How can Alif Visa help with your Hong Kong visit visa?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping travellers worldwide. We can:

  • check your forms, documents and photo before you submit
  • help you write a clear cover letter
  • arrange flight reservations and hotel bookings for your file

ImmD makes every decision, and no one can guarantee a visa. For general entry rules, read our Hong Kong visa overview, or check your route to see your options.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Is a Hong Kong visit visa the same as a China visa?

No. Hong Kong has its own immigration rules. A mainland China visa does not let you enter Hong Kong, and a Hong Kong visit visa does not let you enter mainland China.

Can I apply for a Hong Kong visit visa online?

Yes. ImmD accepts visit and transit visa applications online through GovHK, and you can pay the fee by card.

Do I need a sponsor for a Hong Kong visit visa?

No, a sponsor is optional. It can make your application easier to verify, especially for family or business visits.

How long does a Hong Kong visit visa take?

ImmD normally needs about four weeks after it has every document. Apply at least six weeks before you travel.

Can I work on a Hong Kong visit visa?

No. Visitors may not take paid or unpaid work, start or join a business, or enrol as students.

What does the Hong Kong e-Visa look like?

It is an electronic document with a QR code. Keep it on your phone or print it on A4 paper and show it with your passport at the immigration counter.

Can I extend my stay in Hong Kong?

Extensions are possible in some cases. Apply to ImmD before your permitted stay ends, and explain why you need more time.

What if my Hong Kong visit visa is refused?

Read the reason, fix the weak points such as proof of money or purpose, and reapply with stronger documents.

title: How Do You Book a Qatar Biometric Appointment at a Qatar Visa Center?

desc: Qatar biometric appointment guide: who needs one, how to book at a Qatar Visa Center (QVC) with your visa reference number, and what happens on the day.

content:
Short answer: A Qatar biometric appointment is the in-person visit where your fingerprints and photo are taken for a Qatar work visa. It usually happens at a Qatar Visa Center (QVC) in your home country. Your employer first applies to Qatar's Ministry of Interior and gets a visa reference number. You then book your Qatar biometric appointment online with that number, attend for biometrics, a medical check and contract signing, and wait for the visa.

Quick factsDetails
Who runs itQatar Visa Center (QVC), set up by Qatar's Ministry of Interior
Who needs itMainly people coming to Qatar on a work visa from countries with a QVC
What you need to bookVisa reference number from your employer, plus your passport
What happens thereDocument check, e-signing your contract, fingerprints and photo, medical check
Official sitesqatarvisacenter.com and the Ministry of Interior (Metrash app)

What is a Qatar biometric appointment?

A Qatar biometric appointment is a short visit to a Qatar Visa Center where your fingerprints and facial photo are recorded for your visa. Qatar moved this step out of Doha and into workers' home countries. That means your checks are done before you fly, so you can usually start work soon after you land.

At the same Qatar biometric appointment, you also review and e-sign your employment contract and complete a medical examination. In one visit you finish three steps that used to take weeks after arrival.

Who needs a Qatar biometric appointment?

Qatar Visa Centers mainly handle employment visas. You will probably need a Qatar biometric appointment if:

  • a Qatari employer has offered you a job and applied for your work visa
  • you live in a country that has a Qatar Visa Center
  • your employer has sent you a visa reference number and asked you to "complete QVC"

The first centres opened from 2018 in countries that send many workers to Qatar, including Sri Lanka, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, the Philippines, Indonesia and Tunisia. More locations have opened since. Tourists and short-term visitors usually do not need a Qatar biometric appointment; they apply online or enter visa-free where eligible. Our Qatar visa guide covers the visitor routes.

How do you book a Qatar biometric appointment, step by step?

Booking a Qatar biometric appointment is straightforward once your employer has done their part.

  1. Your employer applies first. The employer submits your work visa application through the Ministry of Interior website or the Metrash app.
  2. Get your visa reference number. Once the Ministry gives initial approval, your employer sends you the reference number. You cannot book without it.
  3. Open the official QVC website. Go to qatarvisacenter.com and choose your country and the centre nearest to you. Avoid look-alike sites.
  4. Enter your details. Type your visa reference number and passport number exactly as they appear on your documents.
  5. Pick a date and time. Choose a slot that leaves you time to gather documents.
  6. Save your confirmation. Print it or keep it on your phone. You will need it at the centre.
  7. Attend your Qatar biometric appointment. Arrive early with your original passport and documents.

What should you bring to your Qatar biometric appointment?

Bring everything your employer and the centre ask for. Usually that means:

  • your original passport, valid for at least six months
  • your visa reference number and appointment confirmation
  • copies of educational certificates or experience letters, if your job needs them
  • passport-size photos if requested (see our visa photo guide)
  • any medical records you have been asked to bring, such as vaccination history

Requirements vary by job and nationality. Always follow the exact checklist your employer and the centre send you.

What happens on the day of your Qatar biometric appointment?

Here is what normally happens, in order:

  1. Check-in. Staff validate your reference number and passport.
  2. Document submission. You hand in the documents for your visa file.
  3. Contract review. You read your employment contract, usually in English and your own language, and e-sign it.
  4. Biometrics. Your fingerprints and photo are taken.
  5. Medical examination. You go to the medical section linked to the centre for your health checks.
  6. Finish. You receive a receipt. Your employer is informed of progress.

Plan to spend several hours at the centre, especially in busy periods.

[IMG2]

Why should you read your contract carefully?

At your Qatar biometric appointment you e-sign the contract that will govern your job. Check that these match what you were offered:

  • job title and duties
  • basic salary and allowances
  • working hours and days off
  • contract length and notice period
  • accommodation and transport, if promised

If something is wrong, raise it with your employer before you complete the process. You will receive a copy of the signed contract at the end.

How much does a Qatar biometric appointment cost?

Fees for Qatar Visa Center services are shown on the official QVC website and can differ by country. In many cases the employer covers visa costs, but check this with your employer in writing. Never pay strangers or social media "agents" for a Qatar biometric appointment slot. Booking through the official website is the safe route.

How long does the Qatar visa take after biometrics?

There is no fixed official time. It depends on your medical results, security checks and your employer's processing. Many applicants hear back within a few weeks of their Qatar biometric appointment. Your employer receives the visa and tells you when you can travel.

For online visa routes, our Qatar processing time guide has more detail.

What are the most common Qatar biometric appointment problems?

Most delays come from preventable issues:

  • Booking before the reference number is active. Wait until your employer confirms initial approval.
  • Name mismatches. If your name on the employer's application differs from your passport, ask your employer to fix it before you book.
  • Paying unofficial agents. Appointments sold by strangers may be fake or cancelled.
  • Missing the medical step. Your visa cannot be issued until the medical check is complete.
  • Arriving without originals. Copies alone are not enough.

Can you reschedule a Qatar biometric appointment?

Usually yes. Use the same official QVC website to change your Qatar biometric appointment, subject to available slots. Do it as early as possible, because popular centres fill up quickly.

A real example: a nurse joining a hospital in Doha

Ravi, a nurse in Kochi, accepts a job at a hospital in Doha. The hospital applies for his work visa and sends him a visa reference number. Ravi books his Qatar biometric appointment at the Kochi centre on the official website for the following week.

On the day, he brings his passport, nursing degree, registration certificate and experience letters. He reads the contract carefully, notices the night-shift allowance is missing, and calls his employer, who confirms it in writing before he signs. Biometrics and the medical take most of the morning. Three weeks later his employer tells him the visa is issued.

The lesson: book only on the official site, bring originals, and read the contract before you sign.

What documents might your employer ask for?

Before or during your Qatar biometric appointment, your employer may need extra documents for your file. Common ones include:

  • Educational certificates, often attested by your home country's foreign ministry and the Qatari embassy, for skilled and professional jobs
  • Experience letters from previous employers, on letterhead, with dates and job titles
  • Professional licences for regulated jobs such as nursing, engineering or teaching
  • Police clearance certificate in some cases
  • Marriage certificate if you plan to sponsor your spouse later

Attestation can take weeks, so start early. Ask your employer exactly which documents need attesting and in what order.

What does the medical examination include?

The medical part of your Qatar biometric appointment checks that you are fit to work and do not have certain infectious diseases. It usually includes:

  • a general physical check
  • a chest X-ray
  • blood tests
  • sometimes other tests, depending on your job and age

Results go to the Qatari authorities and your employer. If anything needs a second look, you may be asked to come back. Bring glasses or medical records if you have an existing condition, and answer questions honestly.

QVC process vs the old process in Qatar

This table shows why most employers now prefer the Qatar Visa Center route.

StepThrough a QVC (home country)Old process (in Qatar)
BiometricsBefore you fly, at your Qatar biometric appointmentAfter arrival
Medical checkBefore you flyAfter arrival, at a medical commission
ContractReviewed and e-signed before you fly, in your languageOften signed after arrival
Starting workSoon after you landAfter all checks are finished

The biggest benefit is certainty: if something is wrong, you find out at home, before you resign from your current job or book flights.

What happens after you arrive in Qatar?

Once your visa is issued and you land, your employer completes your residence permit, often called the Qatar ID (QID). Because your biometrics and medical were done at your Qatar biometric appointment, this step is usually much quicker. Keep copies of your contract, visa and receipts. You will need the QID for things like a bank account, a phone contract and sponsoring family later.

Where are Qatar Visa Centers located?

Qatar has opened visa centres in several countries that send many workers to Doha. The network has grown since the first centre opened in Colombo in 2018. Locations have included:

CountryExample cities with a Qatar Visa Center
IndiaSeveral cities, including New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kochi, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Lucknow
PakistanKarachi and Islamabad
BangladeshDhaka
NepalKathmandu
Sri LankaColombo
PhilippinesManila
IndonesiaJakarta
TunisiaTunis

Centres open, move and change hours, so always confirm the current list on the official QVC website before you book your Qatar biometric appointment.

What questions should you ask your employer first?

A short conversation with your employer before your Qatar biometric appointment saves a lot of stress. Ask:

  1. Has the Ministry of Interior given initial approval, and is my visa reference number active?
  2. Which documents must be attested, and by whom?
  3. Who pays the QVC and medical fees?
  4. Which contract version will I see at the centre, and can I have a copy now to read?
  5. How will you tell me the visa is ready, and who books my flight?
  6. What happens if the medical needs a retest?

Get important answers in writing, by email or message, so you can refer to them later.

What if there is a problem with your medical result?

Sometimes a medical result needs a second test, or a condition needs treatment before the visa can be approved. If that happens:

  • stay calm and ask the centre or your employer exactly what is needed
  • complete any retest or treatment as soon as you can
  • keep all medical reports and receipts

Some conditions can prevent a work visa being issued. If that happens, ask your employer about your options, and keep copies of everything in case you apply again later.

Common myths about the Qatar biometric appointment

"An agent can get me a faster slot for a fee." Slots are released on the official website. Paying an unofficial agent does not speed up the Ministry's decision and can expose your passport details to fraud.

"Biometrics means my visa is approved." Your Qatar biometric appointment is one step. The visa is only issued after the medical, security checks and your employer's final steps are complete.

"I can sign the contract now and change it in Qatar." The contract you e-sign at the centre is the one on file. If something is wrong, fix it with your employer before you sign, not after you land.

"Tourists need a QVC appointment too." Most visitors use Qatar's online visa routes or visa-free entry. The Qatar biometric appointment is mainly for employment visas.

"I can send someone else." Biometrics are personal. You must attend your Qatar biometric appointment yourself, with your original passport.

Tips for a smooth Qatar biometric appointment

  • Book as soon as your reference number is active; slots fill up.
  • Double-check the spelling of your name on every document.
  • Bring originals and one set of copies.
  • Eat beforehand unless you are told to fast for blood tests.
  • Keep your phone charged and your employer's contact details handy.
  • Read the contract slowly, and ask questions before you sign.

How can Alif Visa help?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company that helps applicants around the world understand each step. We can:

  • explain what your employer should send you before your Qatar biometric appointment
  • check your documents and certificates
  • help with visitor visas for family members

For a work visa, your employer must start the application with Qatar's Ministry of Interior. If you're unsure where you stand, talk to our team or check your route.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Can I book a Qatar biometric appointment without a visa reference number?

No. The booking system asks for the visa reference number your employer receives from Qatar's Ministry of Interior.

Is a Qatar biometric appointment needed for tourists?

Generally no. Qatar Visa Centers focus on employment visas. Tourists usually use Qatar's online visa routes or visa-free entry where eligible.

What happens at a Qatar Visa Center?

Your passport and documents are checked, you e-sign your employment contract, your fingerprints and photo are taken, and you complete a medical check.

Can I change my Qatar biometric appointment?

Usually yes, through the same official booking website, subject to available slots.

Do I pay for a Qatar biometric appointment?

Check the official Qatar Visa Center website for current fees, and confirm with your employer who pays. Avoid anyone selling appointments.

How long does the Qatar work visa take after biometrics?

There is no fixed time. Many applicants hear back within a few weeks, depending on medical results and employer processing.

Can my family use the Qatar Visa Center?

Family visas follow different routes, usually sponsored by you once you have your residence permit in Qatar.

content:
Short answer: To check your Sweden visa status for a visitor (Schengen) visa, use the tracking page of the visa centre where you applied, usually VFS Global, with your reference number and date of birth. The Swedish embassy or consulate makes the decision. Most short-stay visas are decided within 15 calendar days, but it can take up to 45 days if extra checks are needed. Work, study and family permits are different: you follow those through the Swedish Migration Agency's e-services.

Who decides visitor visasThe Swedish embassy or consulate, or a country representing Sweden
Where to check Sweden visa statusThe visa centre where you applied, usually VFS Global
What you needReference or tracking number and date of birth
Normal decision timeUp to 15 calendar days, sometimes up to 45
Residence permitsSwedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket) e-services

[IMG1]

What does Sweden visa status mean?

Your Sweden visa status shows where your passport and application are in the process. It tells you whether the file has been received at the visa centre, sent to the embassy, decided, or returned for collection. It normally does not say whether the visa was approved. "Decision made" or "processed" can mean approval or refusal; you find out when you open the envelope.

Knowing this avoids a lot of worry. A Sweden visa status that has not changed for a few days is normal while the embassy is working on your file.

Who decides a Swedish visitor visa?

Short-stay Schengen visas for Sweden are decided by the Swedish embassy or consulate responsible for the country where you live. In some countries, another Schengen country represents Sweden and makes the decision on its behalf. Visa centres such as VFS Global only collect applications, take fingerprints and return passports. They cannot speed up or influence a decision.

The Swedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket) handles residence permits for work, study and family, and acts as the appeal body for some decisions. It does not normally show the Sweden visa status of a tourist or business visitor visa.

How do you check your Sweden visa status, step by step?

Here are five easy ways to stay on top of your Sweden visa status.

  1. Find your reference number. It is printed on the receipt or email the visa centre gave you when you gave your fingerprints.
  2. Use the online tracker. Open the Sweden page of VFS Global for the country where you applied and choose "Track your application". Enter your reference number and date of birth exactly as on the receipt.
  3. Read the stage. Typical stages are "received at the visa centre", "forwarded to the embassy", "processed at the embassy" and "ready for collection" or "dispatched by courier".
  4. Turn on SMS or email updates. Many centres offer paid SMS alerts, so you do not need to keep checking your Sweden visa status by hand.
  5. Contact the visa centre if needed. If the tracker shows an error, the visa centre's helpline or email can confirm where your passport is.

What do the Sweden visa status messages mean?

Status messageWhat it meansWhat you should do
Application received at the visa centreYour file and biometrics were acceptedWait; nothing to do yet
Forwarded to the embassyYour passport and file are with the decision-makersWait for the decision
Processed at the embassyA decision has been madeWait for your passport to return
Ready for collectionYour passport is back at the centreCollect it with your receipt and ID
Dispatched by courierYour passport is on its way to youTrack the courier

How long does a Sweden visitor visa take?

Under the EU Visa Code, consulates aim to decide short-stay visas within 15 calendar days of receiving a complete application. In individual cases, especially when more documents or checks are needed, this can be extended to 45 days. Busy seasons, such as summer and the weeks before Christmas, are often slower.

You can apply up to six months before your trip and no later than 15 days before. The safest window is three to six weeks ahead. Our Sweden visa guide explains the full process.

[IMG2]

What if your Sweden visa status has not changed for weeks?

A Sweden visa status stuck at "forwarded to the embassy" for more than 15 days is worth looking into. Work through these steps:

  • Check your email and spam folder. The embassy may have asked for more documents.
  • Make sure you are on the right website. Sweden uses different visa centres in different countries.
  • Contact the visa centre first. They can see the handover and courier history.
  • Contact the embassy only after 15 days. Have your reference number, passport number and travel date ready. Be polite and brief.
  • Do not book non-refundable travel until your passport is back.

How do you check a Swedish residence permit status?

Work, study and family residence permits are decided by the Swedish Migration Agency. If you applied online, you follow your case by logging in to its e-services with your case number. The Agency also publishes typical processing times for each permit type. This is a different system from the Sweden visa status of a short Schengen visit.

What happens after the decision?

When your passport comes back:

  1. If approved, check the visa sticker carefully: your name, passport number, dates of validity, number of entries and number of days allowed. Report any mistake straight away.
  2. If refused, you receive a standard refusal form listing the reasons and how to appeal. Read it carefully before deciding whether to appeal or reapply.

Many refusals come from weak proof of money, unclear travel plans or doubts about your return home. Our guides on cover letters and Schengen applications help you build a stronger file.

How can you avoid delays in the first place?

A complete file is the best way to keep your Sweden visa status moving.

  • Use the official checklist for your country and visa type.
  • Make sure your passport is valid for at least three months after your trip and has two blank pages.
  • Buy travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover for the whole Schengen area.
  • Provide recent bank statements showing regular income and enough money for your stay.
  • Add a short cover letter that explains your trip, who is paying and why you will return home.
  • Book your appointment early in the morning slots if you can.

Can you travel while your passport is at the embassy?

No, unless you hold a second valid passport. Your passport stays with the visa centre and embassy until the decision is made. Plan your application so you do not need to travel during processing. If an emergency comes up, contact the visa centre to ask whether you can withdraw your application and collect your passport.

A real example: checking a visitor visa in Nairobi

Grace in Nairobi applies for a Sweden visitor visa to attend her sister's wedding in Gothenburg. She gives her fingerprints at the VFS Global centre and keeps the receipt. Each morning she checks her Sweden visa status online. For nine days it reads "forwarded to the embassy". On day ten it changes to "processed at the embassy", and two days later to "ready for collection". She collects her passport and finds a single-entry visa covering the wedding dates. Because her file was complete, she never needed to contact anyone.

Which mistakes slow down a Sweden visa status?

  • Using a tracking website that is not the official visa centre
  • Missing an email asking for more documents
  • Applying with an insurance policy that does not cover the full trip
  • Giving bank statements that show sudden large deposits
  • Applying only a few days before the trip

Sweden visa status vs Schengen rules

A visa issued by Sweden is a Schengen visa. If approved, it usually allows travel to other Schengen countries during its validity, as long as Sweden is your main destination. The 90-days-in-180 rule still applies. Your Sweden visa status page only covers the application; once you have the visa, the rules on the sticker are what matter.

Sweden visa status for family, business and student trips

The way you check your Sweden visa status is the same for every short-stay purpose, but what the embassy looks at differs:

  • Family visits: an invitation from your relative in Sweden, a copy of their ID or residence permit, and proof of your relationship. If they pay for the trip, their bank statements too.
  • Business trips: an invitation letter from the Swedish company, a letter from your employer, and proof of who pays.
  • Short courses (under 90 days): an enrolment letter and proof of fees paid. Courses longer than 90 days need a residence permit from the Swedish Migration Agency, which is tracked in its e-services rather than as a Sweden visa status at a visa centre.

Matching your documents to your purpose is the simplest way to avoid "additional documents requested" delays.

How does Sweden visa status work if another country represents Sweden?

In some countries Sweden has no consulate of its own, so another Schengen country decides visas for Sweden. In that case, you still apply through the visa centre named on the Swedish embassy website, and you still check your Sweden visa status on that centre's tracker. The decision letter may carry the representing country's details. That is normal and does not change what the visa allows.

Sweden visa status and data privacy

Only enter your reference number and date of birth on the official visa centre website. Third-party "visa status checker" websites cannot see embassy systems. Some collect personal data or charge for information you can get free. If a website asks for card details just to show your Sweden visa status, close it.

How can Alif Visa help?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company working with applicants around the world. We prepare and check Schengen visa files before you submit, help you book appointments and arrange insurance that meets Schengen rules. The embassy always makes the final decision.

Already applied with us? Use Track application to see our stage, or check your route for a new trip.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Can I check my Sweden visa status online?

Yes. Use the tracking page of the visa centre where you applied, usually VFS Global, with your reference number and date of birth.

Does Migrationsverket show Sweden visa status for visitor visas?

Normally no. Visitor visas are decided by the embassy and tracked through the visa centre. Migrationsverket e-services are for residence permits.

How long does a Sweden Schengen visa take?

Usually up to 15 calendar days after a complete application, and up to 45 days in some cases.

What does "processed at the embassy" mean?

The embassy has made a decision and your passport is on its way back to the visa centre. You find out the result when you collect it.

Can I travel while my passport is at the embassy?

No, not unless you have a second valid passport.

Who do I contact if my Sweden visa status has not changed?

Start with the visa centre. Contact the embassy only if it has been more than 15 days and the centre cannot help.

Can I appeal a Sweden visa refusal?

Yes. The refusal form explains how and by when to appeal. You can also reapply with a stronger file.

title: How Do You Book a BLS Visa Appointment?
seo_title: BLS Appointment: 7 Easy Steps to Book a BLS International Visa Slot (2026)
desc: BLS appointment guide: how to book a BLS International visa appointment, mainly for Spain, what to bring, fees, and how to avoid fake booking agents.
alt1: bls appointment guide with Plaza Mayor in Madrid
content:
Short answer: A BLS appointment is a booked time at a BLS International visa application centre, where you hand in your visa documents and give your fingerprints. BLS collects applications for some governments, most often Spain. To book a appointment, open the official BLS website for your country and the embassy you are applying to, create an account, fill in your details, choose a centre and time, and print the confirmation. Booking on the official site is free; you pay the official fees when you submit.

Quick factsDetails
What BLS isA private visa application centre company working for embassies
Best known forSpain visa applications in many countries, including the UK and UAE
Who decides your visaThe embassy or consulate, not BLS
Booking costFree on the official BLS site; visa and service fees are paid at submission
What to bringAppointment letter, passport, completed form, photo and supporting documents

Table of Contents

  • What is a BLS appointment?
  • Who needs a BLS appointment?
  • How do you book a BLS appointment, step by step?
  • What should you bring on the day?
  • How much does it cost to apply through BLS?
  • Can a travel agent book for you?
  • What if there are no slots available?
  • What happens at the visa centre?
  • How do you track your application afterwards?
  • A real example: a BLS appointment in Dubai
  • Which mistakes should you avoid?
  • BLS appointment vs VFS Global vs TLScontact
  • Tips to make your BLS appointment quick
  • Can BLS handle long-stay visas?
  • Is BLS safe for your passport and data?
  • What if you miss your BLS appointment?
  • How can Alif Visa help with your BLS appointment?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Sources
[IMG1]

What is a BLS appointment?

A BLS appointment is your slot at a BLS International centre to submit a visa application in person. At the appointment, staff check your documents, take your fingerprints and photo, collect the fees and send your file to the embassy. BLS only handles the paperwork. The embassy or consulate decides whether you get the visa.

BLS International works for several governments. It is best known for Spain: in many countries, every Spain visa application goes through a BLS appointment. In the UK, for example, BLS runs Spain visa centres for UK residents, and in the UAE it runs the Spain centres in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

Who needs a BLS appointment?

You need a BLS appointment if the embassy you are applying to uses BLS International in the country where you live. Check the embassy's website first. It will say whether it uses BLS, VFS Global, TLScontact or its own office. You usually need one if you are:

  • applying for a Spain Schengen visa (tourism, business, family visit or study) in a country where Spain uses BLS
  • applying for a Spanish national (long-stay) visa where BLS collects applications
  • giving biometrics for a visa that requires fingerprints

British citizens do not need a visa for short visits to Spain, so they usually do not need a BLS appointment unless they apply for a long-stay visa.

How do you book a BLS appointment, step by step?

Booking a BLS appointment takes about 20 minutes if you have your passport and travel dates ready.

  1. Confirm BLS handles your application. Check the embassy website for the country you are visiting.
  2. Open the official BLS site for your country of residence. Each country has its own BLS website or section.
  3. Create an account with your email and phone number. Many BLS sites now link each appointment to your passport number.
  4. Choose your visa category (tourism, business, family visit, study and so on) and fill in your details.
  5. Pick the centre for your area. Embassies divide countries into jurisdictions, so you must use the centre that covers where you live.
  6. Select a date and time for your appointment, then confirm.
  7. Print the appointment letter or save it on your phone, and bring it with your original documents.

What should you bring on the day?

Bring originals and one set of copies of everything. For a Spain Schengen visa, that usually means:

  • Appointment confirmation letter from the official BLS site
  • Passport valid for at least three months after your trip, with two blank pages, issued within the last ten years
  • Completed and signed application form
  • A recent passport photo that meets Schengen rules (see our visa photo guide)
  • Proof of residence in the country where you apply, if you are not a citizen, such as a residence permit
  • Travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover for the whole Schengen area
  • Flight and hotel reservations or an invitation letter
  • Bank statements for the last three to six months and an employment or study letter
  • A short cover letter explaining your trip
  • Payment for the visa fee and the BLS service fee
[IMG2]

How much does it cost to apply through BLS?

Booking a BLS appointment on the official website is free. When you submit your application, you pay:

  • the visa fee, set by the EU for Schengen visas (currently €90 for adults, with lower fees for children)
  • the BLS service fee, which varies by country
  • optional extras, such as SMS updates, courier return, photocopies or a premium lounge

Anyone asking you to pay just to book a BLS appointment is not BLS. Do not pay them.

Can a travel agent book for you?

It depends on the country. In the UAE, BLS announced in July 2026 that Spain visa appointments must be self-booked, are tied to the applicant's passport number, and appointments obtained through agents or third parties are not accepted at the centres. BLS also said booking on its website is free and payment happens at submission.

Wherever you live, be careful with anyone selling "guaranteed" BLS appointment slots on social media or unofficial websites. Your appointment may be cancelled at the door, and your passport details may be misused.

What if there are no slots available?

Slots can be hard to find in busy seasons. These tips help:

  • Check early in the morning and at the start of each week, when new slots are often released.
  • Look at other centres in your jurisdiction, if you are allowed to use them.
  • Apply earlier. Schengen visas can be requested up to six months before travel.
  • Keep your account logged in and your documents ready, so you can book quickly.
  • Never buy appointments from unofficial sellers.

What happens at the visa centre?

On the day of your appointment:

  1. Arrive early. Security checks can take time, and late arrivals may be turned away.
  2. Check in with your appointment letter and passport.
  3. Submit your documents. Staff check that the file is complete. They may tell you if something is missing.
  4. Give biometrics. Your fingerprints and photo are taken, unless you gave them in the last 59 months for a Schengen visa.
  5. Pay the fees and choose any optional services.
  6. Receive a receipt with your tracking number. Keep it safe.

How do you track your application afterwards?

Use the tracking tool on the same BLS website with the reference number on your receipt. Typical stages are "received", "sent to the consulate", "processed" and "ready for collection" or "dispatched". When your passport is ready, collect it in person or receive it by courier. If the visa is refused, the refusal letter explains why and how to appeal.

A real example: a BLS appointment in Dubai

Omar is an engineer living in Dubai, and he wants to visit Barcelona for a conference. He opens the official BLS Spain website for the UAE, creates an account linked to his passport, and books a BLS appointment at the Dubai centre for a Tuesday morning. He brings his Emirates ID copy, a no-objection letter signed by his manager with her full name, job title and Emirates ID number, his salary certificate, six months of bank statements, his conference invitation, his hotel booking and his travel insurance. The appointment takes 40 minutes. He tracks his application online and collects his passport with a visa two weeks later.

Which mistakes should you avoid?

  • Booking through social media sellers instead of the official site
  • Choosing the wrong visa category or the wrong centre for your area
  • Missing originals, such as your residence permit
  • Bringing travel insurance that does not cover the whole Schengen area
  • Arriving late or without the appointment letter
  • Unsigned employer letters, which some centres now reject

BLS appointment vs VFS Global vs TLScontact

Three companies handle most visa applications for European embassies. Which one you use depends on the embassy and the country you live in, not on your choice.

CompanyCommon examplesWho decides the visa
BLS InternationalSpain in many countriesThe embassy or consulate
VFS GlobalMany Schengen countries, the UK, Canada and others in many countriesThe embassy or consulate
TLScontactFrance, Belgium and others in many countriesThe embassy or consulate

The process is similar at all three: book online, attend in person, give biometrics, track your passport. Always use the company named on the embassy's own website.

Tips to make your BLS appointment quick

  • Fill in the online form completely before the day, so staff only need to check it.
  • Put documents in the order of the official checklist.
  • Bring a pen, copies and the exact visa category printed on your appointment letter.
  • Wear something without a hood or hat, because your photo may be taken.
  • Bring payment in the method the centre accepts; some centres do not take every card.
  • If you apply as a family, book a BLS appointment for each person, or a group booking where the site allows it.

Can BLS handle long-stay visas?

Yes, in many countries. Spanish national visas, such as study, work, family reunification or non-lucrative residence visas, are often collected through a BLS appointment too. These files are longer and may need apostilled and translated documents, police certificates and medical certificates. The categories appear separately on the booking site, so choose carefully. A long-stay visa is decided by the consulate and can take several weeks, much longer than a Schengen visit visa.

Is BLS safe for your passport and data?

BLS International is contracted by the embassy to collect applications, and its centres follow the embassy's rules on data and document handling. Your passport is kept securely and returned by hand or by tracked courier. To stay safe, only share your details on the official BLS website, keep your receipt, and never hand your passport to anyone outside the centre who offers to "help" with your BLS appointment.

What if you miss your BLS appointment?

If you cannot attend, cancel or reschedule your appointment through your account as early as possible. Missed appointments may not be refunded, and some systems limit how often you can rebook. If you arrive very late, the centre may refuse to see you and ask you to book again.

How can Alif Visa help with your BLS appointment?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping travellers worldwide. We help you choose the right visa category, check your documents and prepare your file before your appointment. We also arrange travel insurance, flight reservations and hotel bookings for your application. The embassy always makes the final decision.

Read our Spain visa guide, see our visa appointment service, or check your route.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

Is BLS the Spanish embassy?

No. BLS International is a private company that collects applications for the embassy. The embassy or consulate makes the visa decision.

Is booking a BLS appointment free?

Yes, on the official BLS website. You pay the visa fee and the BLS service fee when you submit your application.

Can I reschedule my BLS appointment?

Usually yes, through your account on the same website, depending on available slots and local rules.

Which countries use BLS International?

BLS works for several governments and is best known for Spain visa applications in many countries. Check your destination embassy's website to see who handles applications where you live.

Can I apply at any BLS centre?

No. You must use the centre that covers the area where you legally live.

Do I need to give fingerprints at every BLS appointment?

Not always. If you gave Schengen fingerprints in the last 59 months, you may not need to give them again.

How long after my BLS appointment will I get my passport?

Most Schengen visa decisions take up to 15 calendar days, plus a few days to return your passport.

title: What Size Is an Australia Visa Photo?

alt1: australia visa photo guide with Sydney Opera House
content:
Short answer: An Australia visa photo should be a recent colour photo of your face against a plain light background. For printed photos, the size is 35 to 40 mm wide and 45 to 50 mm high, so a standard 35 x 45 mm passport photo works. Most Australian visas are now applied for online in ImmiAccount, where you upload a clear digital Australia visa photo instead of posting a printed one.

Quick factsDetails
Printed size35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high
Head sizeChin to crown about 32-36 mm
Age of photoTaken in the last 6 months
BackgroundPlain, light-coloured, no shadows
ExpressionNeutral, mouth closed, eyes open
Online applicationsUpload a JPG in ImmiAccount

Table of Contents

  • Do you also need biometrics for an Australian visa?

[IMG1]

What is an Australia visa photo?

An Australia visa photo is a recent passport-style photo that the Department of Home Affairs uses to identify you. It is matched against your passport and, for many visas, against the facial image taken at the border. A clear photo helps your application move without questions.

For most online visas, such as the visitor visa (subclass 600), the student visa or the work visas, you upload your Australia visa photo as a file. Some paper forms, citizenship applications and in-person services still ask for printed photos.

What size is an Australia visa photo?

For printed photos, Australia uses the same size as an Australian passport photo:

  • Width: 35 to 40 mm
  • Height: 45 to 50 mm
  • Face: from chin to the top of the head roughly 32 to 36 mm

A standard 35 x 45 mm photo from a photo shop meets these limits. For a digital Australia visa photo, there is no fixed size in millimetres. Instead, the file must be clear, in colour, show your face properly and stay within the upload limits shown in ImmiAccount.

What are the 10 rules for an Australia visa photo?

Follow these ten rules and your Australia visa photo will almost always be accepted.

  1. Recent: taken within the last six months, so it looks like you now.
  2. In colour: no black-and-white photos, filters or beauty edits.
  3. Plain light background: white, cream or light grey, with no patterns, objects or other people.
  4. Even lighting: no shadows on your face or behind your head.
  5. Face the camera: look straight at the lens with your head level.
  6. Neutral expression: mouth closed, eyes open, no wide smile.
  7. Full face visible: from the top of your hair to your chin, with the edges of your face showing.
  8. No sunglasses or tinted lenses: clear glasses only if you must wear them, with no glare.
  9. Head coverings for religious or medical reasons only: your full face must still be visible.
  10. Sharp and in focus: no blur, no pixelation, no photo of a photo.

How do you upload an Australia visa photo in ImmiAccount?

Here is how to add your Australia visa photo to an online application.

  1. Take the photo against a plain wall in good daylight. Ask someone else to take it from about one to two metres away.
  2. Check it on a computer. Your whole face and the top of your shoulders should be visible and sharp.
  3. Crop it so your head is centred, with a little space above it. Do not stretch or squash the image.
  4. Save it as a JPG under the file size limit shown on the upload screen.
  5. Log in to ImmiAccount, open your application and go to "Attach documents".
  6. Choose the photo document type, for example "Photograph - Passport", and upload the file.
  7. Submit and keep a copy of your Australia visa photo for future applications.

If you are applying through a visa centre in person, staff may also take a photo of you there. Bring a printed one anyway if the checklist asks for it.

[IMG2]

Can you take an Australia visa photo with your phone?

Yes. A modern phone takes a perfectly good Australia visa photo if you follow a few tips:

  • Use the rear camera, not the selfie camera, and ask someone else to take it.
  • Stand facing a window for soft, even daylight.
  • Stand about half a metre in front of a plain wall, so you do not cast a shadow on it.
  • Turn off portrait mode and beauty filters.
  • Hold the phone at eye level, not above or below your face.

Take several shots and pick the sharpest one.

What are the most common Australia visa photo mistakes?

These are the problems that most often get photos questioned:

  • A selfie taken at arm's length, which distorts the face
  • Shadows behind the head or across the face
  • The chin or top of the hair cut off
  • An old photo that no longer looks like you
  • Smiling widely, tilting the head, or wearing a hat or sunglasses
  • A photo of a printed photo, which looks blurry
  • Heavy filters or edited skin
  • A busy background, such as a bookshelf or curtain pattern

Do children need an Australia visa photo?

Yes. Every applicant, including babies, needs their own Australia visa photo. The same rules apply, with some flexibility for very young children:

  • Lay a baby on a plain light sheet and take the photo from above.
  • Their eyes should be open if possible.
  • No hands, toys or dummies should be in the shot.
  • Older children should look at the camera with a neutral expression.

Australia visa photo vs Australian passport photo

The two are very similar, but there are differences in how they are used.

Australia visa photoAustralian passport photo
Who needs itVisa applicants (non-citizens)Australian citizens
Usual formatDigital upload in ImmiAccountPrinted or digital, depending on the application
Printed size35-40 mm x 45-50 mm35-40 mm x 45-50 mm
Checked byDepartment of Home AffairsAustralian Passport Office

If you already have a good passport-style photo taken in the last six months, you can usually use it as your Australia visa photo too.

What happens if your Australia visa photo is not accepted?

Home Affairs may contact you to ask for a new photo. This can slow your application down, especially for visitor visas where processing is otherwise quick. Reply quickly with a photo that follows the rules above. Keep an eye on your ImmiAccount messages and email, including the spam folder.

Do you also need biometrics for an Australian visa?

Some applicants must give biometrics, which means fingerprints and a facial photo taken at an Australian Visa Application Centre. This depends on your nationality, where you apply and the visa type. If you are asked to give biometrics, you will get a letter in ImmiAccount. The photo taken there is separate from the Australia visa photo you upload.

A real example: a family visitor visa

Maria from Manila is applying for a visitor visa to see her daughter in Brisbane, together with her husband and their 4-year-old grandson. Each person needs their own Australia visa photo. Maria's daughter takes the photos at home against a white wall in the morning light, using the rear camera of her phone. For the little boy she uses a white sheet and takes several shots until he looks at the camera with his mouth closed. She crops each image, saves them as JPGs and uploads them to each person's application in ImmiAccount. The applications are decided without any request for new photos.

Which Australian visas need a photo?

Almost every Australian visa application asks for an Australia visa photo. Common examples:

VisaHow the photo is usually provided
Visitor visa (subclass 600)Digital upload in ImmiAccount
Student visa (subclass 500)Digital upload in ImmiAccount
Temporary Skill Shortage and skilled work visasDigital upload in ImmiAccount
Partner and family visasDigital upload, sometimes printed photos for forms
Paper forms such as Form 1229 or citizenship formsPrinted photos, signed on the back where asked

Always follow the document checklist for your exact visa subclass, because it tells you whether you need digital, printed or both.

How do you make a good photo at home?

You do not need a studio to take a good Australia visa photo. Set up like this:

  • Wall: pick a plain white or light grey wall with no pictures, switches or shadows.
  • Light: face a window on a bright day, or use two lamps either side of the camera to avoid harsh shadows.
  • Distance: stand about half a metre from the wall and have the camera about one to two metres from you.
  • Height: the camera lens should be level with your eyes.
  • Clothing: wear something in a colour that stands out from the wall, without a hood or uniform-style cap.
  • Hair: keep hair away from your eyes and the edges of your face.

Check the result at full size. If your eyes are not sharp, take it again.

Printed photos: what else should you know?

If a paper form asks for a printed Australia visa photo, use good-quality photo paper and do not cut it smaller than 35 mm wide. Some forms ask you or a witness to write your name on the back. Use a soft pen so it does not press through. Never staple through your face; clip the photo to the corner of the page instead.

Does the photo need to match your passport?

How do you get an Azerbaijan visa, step by step?

  2. Go to the official portal, evisa.gov.az. Look-alike websites charge extra and some are scams.
  3. Fill in the form with your passport details, travel dates and the address where you will stay.
  4. Upload a passport scan of your photo page, clear and with all four corners visible.
  5. Choose standard or urgent processing and pay by card. The fee is shown before you pay.
  6. Receive your visa by email and check every detail matches your passport.
  7. Travel with a printed copy or a copy on your phone, plus your return ticket and accommodation details.

Missing registration can lead to a fine when you leave, so check the current rule before your trip.

What documents should you carry with your Azerbaijan visa?

  • your passport, valid beyond your stay
  • your printed or digital Azerbaijan visa
  • a return or onward ticket
  • your hotel booking or host's address
  • travel insurance, which is strongly recommended

Keep copies of everything on your phone and in your luggage.

Can you get an Azerbaijan visa on arrival?

James from Manchester plans four days in Baku for a friend's wedding. Ten days before travel he opens evisa.gov.az, completes the form with his hotel address, uploads a scan of his passport and pays for standard processing. Two working days later his Azerbaijan visa arrives by email. He prints two copies, keeps a PDF on his phone and shows it with his passport at Heydar Aliyev International Airport. Because he stays in a hotel for under 15 days, he does not need to register himself.

  • Gobustan: rock carvings and mud volcanoes south of Baku
  • Sheki: a mountain town known for its Khan's Palace and caravanserais
  • Gabala: mountain scenery and resorts popular in summer and winter

You cannot work, study long-term or take paid assignments. If your trip changes, for example from a holiday to a job offer, you need a different Azerbaijan visa.

Is travel insurance needed for an Azerbaijan visa?

Healthcare in Baku can be expensive for foreigners, and travel outside the capital may mean long journeys to a hospital. Keep your policy number and the insurer's emergency phone number with your visa.

Business trips: what extra do you need?

  • a letter from your UK employer explaining the trip
  • an invitation from the company or event in Azerbaijan
  • your conference registration or meeting schedule

If you will be paid by an Azerbaijani company or work on a project there, ask your host whether you need a work permit and a different Azerbaijan visa.

Travelling with children

Each child needs their own Azerbaijan visa, applied for with their own passport. If a child travels with only one parent, carry a consent letter from the other parent with a copy of their passport. If a child travels with grandparents or another adult, carry a consent letter from both parents. Birth certificates help prove the relationship.

What if your Azerbaijan visa application is refused or delayed?

If an application is refused, check that your details match your passport exactly and that you used the right visa type. You can usually apply again with corrected information. What is a Bahrain visa?

A Bahrain visit visa covers tourism, visiting friends and family, and short business trips. It does not allow you to work. For work or long stays you need a work visa and residence permit, usually arranged by an employer.

Do British citizens need a Bahrain visa?

Yes. A British passport does not give visa-free entry to Bahrain, but British citizens are among the nationalities that can get a visa easily. According to GOV.UK, you can get one:

  • online in advance through the official eVisa portal
  • in advance from the Bahrain Embassy in London
  • on arrival at Bahrain International Airport

The eVisa is the most convenient choice for most travellers because you arrive with your visa already approved.

Do UK residents with other passports need a Bahrain visa?

It depends on your nationality, not where you live. Bahrain sets its rules by passport:

  • Some nationalities can use the eVisa portal directly.
  • Some can get a visa on arrival.
  • Some need a sponsor in Bahrain or an embassy application.
  • Some nationalities may qualify for easier eVisa options if they hold certain residence permits or visas, such as a UK residence permit.

Use the eligibility tool on evisa.gov.bh with your own passport, or read our Bahrain visa guide for nationality-specific rules.

How do you apply for a Bahrain visa, step by step?

Here are six easy ways to make your visa application smooth.

  1. Check your passport. It must be valid for at least six months from the day you arrive.
  2. Choose your option: eVisa online, the embassy, or a visa on arrival.
  3. For the eVisa, go to evisa.gov.bh. Pick the visit visa type that matches your trip and length of stay.
  4. Fill in the form and upload documents. Usually a passport scan and photo, and sometimes a return ticket and hotel booking.
  5. Pay the fee shown on the portal by card.

What documents do you need for a Bahrain visa?

For a standard Bahrain visa, expect to provide:

  • a passport valid for at least six months from arrival
  • a clear passport-style photo (see our visa photo guide)
  • a confirmed return or onward ticket
  • a hotel booking or your host's address
  • proof of enough money for your stay, if asked

For business trips, add an invitation letter from the Bahraini company. For family visits, a letter from your relative and a copy of their ID helps.

How much does a Bahrain visa cost?

How long can you stay on a Bahrain visa?

GOV.UK says a standard Bahrain visa is issued for two weeks. Visit visas for stays of up to six months are also available. Can you extend a Bahrain visa?

Can you visit Bahrain and Saudi Arabia on one trip?

What are the most common Bahrain visa mistakes?

  • Travelling with a passport valid for less than six months
  • Choosing the wrong visa length for your trip
  • Applying through unofficial websites with extra charges
  • Planning to work on a visit visa, which is not allowed
  • Overstaying, which can bring fines and future refusals
  • Forgetting that each family member needs their own Bahrain visa

What should you know about exit restrictions?

GOV.UK warns that you may be stopped from leaving Bahrain if you have a travel ban, legal proceedings or unpaid debts. If you have lived or worked in Bahrain before, you can check for a travel ban through Bahrain's official online services before you travel. Most visitors are never affected, but it is worth knowing.

A real example: a family visit from London

Sana lives in London with a Pakistani passport and a UK residence permit. Her husband Tom is a British citizen. They want to visit Tom's brother in Manama for ten days. Tom applies for a standard Bahrain visa on evisa.gov.bh and gets it in two days. Sana checks the eligibility tool with her own passport, sees she can apply online because of her UK residence permit, and uploads her passport, residence permit and photo. Both visas are approved before they fly, and they enter quickly at Bahrain International Airport.

What can you do in Bahrain on a visit visa?

Bahrain is small, so a short trip covers a lot. Visitors on a visa often enjoy:

  • Bahrain Fort (Qal'at al-Bahrain): a UNESCO World Heritage site with a museum on the island's ancient Dilmun history
  • Manama Souq and Bab Al Bahrain: traditional markets for spices, gold and textiles
  • The Bahrain National Museum and Al Fateh Grand Mosque
  • The Pearling Path in Muharraq: another UNESCO site telling the story of Bahrain's pearl trade
  • The Bahrain International Circuit, home of the Formula 1 Grand Prix

Book early around the Grand Prix weekend, when flights, hotels and visa processing are busier.

Business visits: what extra should you bring?

a visa for business visitors usually needs:

  • an invitation letter from the Bahraini company, with your name, dates and purpose
  • a letter from your UK employer confirming your job and that they pay for the trip
  • your meeting or conference schedule

You can attend meetings, conferences and negotiations. If you will deliver paid work for a Bahraini client, ask whether you need a work permit instead.

When is the best time to visit Bahrain?

The cooler months from November to March are the most comfortable, with warm days and mild evenings. Summer, from June to September, is very hot and humid. Transit through Bahrain

  4. Pay the fee and submit your application.
  5. Wait for the decision and collect your visa or receive it electronically.

Requirements differ a lot between visa types, so read the consulate's checklist carefully.

How do you stay longer than 90 days in Brazil?

Contact Brazil's Federal Police (Polícia Federal) before your 90 days end to ask about an extension. They decide whether you can stay longer. If you overstay, you pay a daily fine when you leave or on your next visit, which can make future trips harder.

What should dual British-Brazilian nationals know?

GOV.UK says Brazilian immigration often requires dual nationals to enter and leave Brazil on a Brazilian passport. If you are a dual national, travel with both passports, use your Brazilian one for Brazil, and your British one for returning to the UK.

Travelling with children to Brazil

Brazil has strict rules for children under 18:

  • children travelling without both parents need authorisation from both parents or guardians
  • non-Brazilian children should carry the original or a notarised copy of their birth certificate
  • Brazilian children may need a specific travel authorisation

Check with the Brazilian consulate before you book, because these rules are enforced at the airport.

Brazil visa vs visa-free: a quick comparison

SituationBrazil visa needed?
British tourist for up to 90 daysNo
British citizen working for a Brazilian companyYes
British student on a full degree in BrazilYes
UK resident with a passport that needs a visaYes, a visitor Brazil visa
Business meetings without payment in BrazilUsually no for British citizens, but check

What are the most common mistakes?

  • Travelling with a passport that expires within six months
  • Not checking for an entry stamp
  • Assuming visa-free entry covers paid work or projects
  • Dual nationals using the wrong passport
  • Children travelling without the right authorisation
  • Bringing US$10,000 or more in cash without declaring it online

A real example: a two-week holiday

Priya, a British citizen from Leeds, books two weeks in Rio and Iguazu. She checks her passport is valid for another two years, books her return flight and hotels, and gets a yellow fever vaccination after reading TravelHealthPro advice for her route. At Rio airport she shows her passport, gets it stamped and enters without any Brazil visa. Her cousin in Leicester has a different passport that needs a visitor visa, so he applies through the consulate six weeks before travel.

Which Brazil visa types exist?

If you need a visa, these are the main categories:

Brazil visa typeWho it is for
Visitor visa (VIVIS)Tourists, business visitors and transit passengers from countries that need a visa
Temporary visa (VITEM)Work, study, research, family reunion, digital nomads, volunteering and similar longer stays
Diplomatic and official visasGovernment officials on duty

Within the temporary category there are many subtypes, each with its own documents. The consulate's list tells you which one fits your plans.

Can you work remotely in Brazil without a Brazil visa?

Working remotely for a UK employer while on holiday in Brazil is a grey area. Brazil offers a temporary Brazil visa for digital nomads who work for foreign employers and meet income requirements. If you plan to spend weeks or months working from Brazil, check the digital nomad route with the consulate rather than relying on visa-free entry.

What should you know about money and health?

  • Cash: bringing US$10,000 or more, or the equivalent, in cash or travellers' cheques requires an online declaration.
  • Insurance: Brazil does not require travel insurance for British tourists, but medical treatment can be expensive. Get cover for medical care and repatriation.
  • Vaccines: yellow fever vaccination is recommended for many areas. Check TravelHealthPro before you go.
  • Safety: follow GOV.UK travel advice for the areas you plan to visit.

How long does a Brazil visa take?

If you do need a visa, processing time depends on the type and on the consulate's workload. Visitor visas are usually faster than temporary residence visas, which can take several weeks because of document checks. Apply as early as the rules allow and avoid booking non-refundable travel until your visa is approved.

Brazil visa rules for UK residents with other passports

If you live in the UK on a residence permit but hold, for example, an Indian, Nigerian or Chinese passport, the visa rules for your nationality apply. Check the consulate's list before booking flights. Where you need a visitor Brazil visa, prepare:

  • your passport and UK residence permit
  • proof of employment or study in the UK
  • recent bank statements
  • your flight and accommodation plans
  • an invitation letter if you are visiting family or a company

Best time to visit Brazil

Brazil is huge, so the best time depends on where you go. Rio de Janeiro and the south-east are warm year-round, with the hottest weather from December to March. The Amazon is wettest from December to May. Carnival in February or March is the busiest period of the year: flights and hotels sell out, so plan early. If you need a visa because of your nationality, apply well before Carnival season.

Entering Brazil overland

You can enter Brazil by land from neighbouring countries such as Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. The same rules apply: British citizens enter visa-free and must get an entry stamp. At smaller crossings, look for the immigration post yourself; if you miss the stamp, you may be fined when you leave Brazil. Travellers who need a visa must have it before reaching the border.

Leaving Brazil and returning to the UK

When you leave Brazil, the officer checks how long you stayed. Keep your boarding pass and passport stamp safe in case of questions. Returning to the UK, you need a valid British passport or a certificate of entitlement. If you lost your passport in Brazil, contact the British Embassy in Brasília or a British consulate for an emergency travel document.

Key takeaways

  • British citizens can visit Brazil visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism.
  • Your passport must be valid for at least six months after arrival, and you must get an entry stamp.
  • Work, study, long stays and remote work need the right Brazil visa.
  • UK residents with other passports follow the rules for their own nationality.
  • Dual nationals should usually use their Brazilian passport in Brazil.
  • Extensions are handled by the Federal Police before your 90 days end.

No. British citizens can visit Brazil visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism.

You can ask the Federal Police before your 90 days end. They decide whether an extension is possible.

title: Do British Citizens Need a Visa for Cambodia?

content:
Short answer: Yes. British citizens need a Cambodia visa to visit. The easiest way is the official Cambodia e-visa, applied for online or through the official app at least four days before you travel. You can also get a Cambodia visa on arrival at airports and land borders, paid in US dollars. A tourist visa allows 30 days from the date you enter and can be extended inside Cambodia.

Quick factsDetails

Tourist stay30 days from entry, extendable in Cambodia
Passport validityAt least 6 months from arrival, undamaged
e-Arrival CardFree, required for arrivals by air at main airports
