What is a Cambodia visa?

A Cambodia visa is permission from the Cambodian government to enter the country. For holidays, the most common type is the tourist visa, valid for 30 days from the day you enter. You can get it as an e-visa before you travel or as a visa on arrival. For work you need a business Cambodia visa and a work permit.

Do British citizens need a Cambodia visa?

Yes. GOV.UK confirms that British citizens need a visa to enter Cambodia as visitors. You have two choices:

  • e-visa: apply online through the official website linked from the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in the UK, or through the official e-visa app, at least four days before you travel
  • visa on arrival: available at international airports and land border crossings, with a photo and payment in US dollars

The e-visa is quicker on arrival because you skip the visa queue.

How do you get a Cambodia visa online, step by step?

Getting your Cambodia visa online is simple if you use the official channel.

  1. Check your passport. It must be valid for at least six months from arrival and not damaged. Cambodia normally refuses entry on damaged passports.
  2. Open the official e-visa website or app, linked from the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in the UK.
  3. Choose the tourist visa and fill in your details exactly as in your passport.
  4. Upload a recent passport-style photo and a scan of your passport if asked.
  5. Pay the fee shown on the official site by card.
  6. Wait at least four days for your Cambodia visa to arrive by email.
  7. Print two copies and carry them with your passport.

How much does a Cambodia visa cost?

The official e-visa site shows the current fee before you pay, including any processing charge. The visa on arrival fee is paid in US dollars in cash, so bring clean, undamaged notes. Look-alike websites often charge much more than the official fee, so check you are on the government site before entering card details.

Can you get a Cambodia visa on arrival?

Yes. If you do not get an e-visa, you can get a Cambodia visa on arrival at international airports and land border crossings. You need:

  • your passport, valid for six months and undamaged
  • a passport photo
  • the fee in US dollars cash
  • the arrival form handed out on the plane or at the border

Queues can be long at busy times, especially at land borders. The e-visa saves time.

[IMG2]

What is the Cambodia e-Arrival Card?

The e-Arrival Card is a free online form for travellers arriving by air at Phnom Penh, Siem Reap or Sihanoukville. Complete it within seven days before your flight. It is separate from your Cambodia visa, so you need both. There is no charge; avoid websites that ask for payment.

How long can you stay in Cambodia?

A tourist Cambodia visa is valid for 30 days from the date of entry. You can extend it while you are in Cambodia through the immigration authorities or a licensed agent. Overstaying brings a fine with no upper limit, possible detention and deportation. If you overstay by more than 30 days, you must leave and pay the fine.

Tourist vs business Cambodia visa

Tourist visaBusiness visa
PurposeHolidays and visiting friendsBusiness, work and longer stays
Initial stay30 days30 days
ExtensionsLimited extensionsLonger extensions possible
Work allowed?NoOnly with a work permit

If you plan to work, volunteer long-term or stay for months, the business Cambodia visa is usually the right starting point.

What else must you do after you arrive?

  • Keep your departure form. You receive it on arrival. If you lose it, contact immigration before leaving.
  • Register your stay. Hotels and landlords register guests automatically. If you stay with friends or family or own a home, register yourself on the official FPCS app using a Cambodian phone number.
  • Carry ID. Keep a copy of your passport and Cambodia visa with you.

What should UK residents with other passports do?

Cambodia's visa rules depend on nationality. Some ASEAN nationals do not need a visa, while most others can use the e-visa. A few nationalities must apply through an embassy. Check your passport on the official e-visa site or our Cambodia visa guide.

Which Cambodia visa mistakes should you avoid?

  • Using look-alike websites that charge extra
  • Applying fewer than four days before travel
  • Travelling with a damaged passport, which can mean refused entry
  • Forgetting the free e-Arrival Card
  • Bringing torn or old US dollar notes for a visa on arrival
  • Overstaying the 30 days

Visiting Angkor and travelling around Cambodia

Most visitors spend time at the Angkor temples near Siem Reap, which need a separate Angkor Pass bought at the official ticket centre or online. Phnom Penh has the Royal Palace and the Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek memorials. The south coast and islands are popular for beach time. Domestic travel is mainly by bus, boat or short flights. Keep your passport and a copy of your Cambodia visa with you, as hotels and guesthouses ask for them.

Combining Cambodia with Thailand or Vietnam

Many travellers visit Cambodia as part of a wider trip. British citizens can usually visit Thailand without a visa for short stays, while Vietnam has its own e-visa system. If you cross a land border into Cambodia, your e-visa must allow entry at that crossing, or you can get a Cambodia visa on arrival there. Check that your chosen border post accepts e-visas before you plan your route.

Health and money tips

  • Currency: the Cambodian riel, but US dollars are widely used. ATMs usually give dollars.
  • Health: check vaccine and malaria advice on TravelHealthPro before you go.
  • Insurance: get travel insurance with medical cover and evacuation, as serious cases may need treatment in Bangkok or Singapore.
  • Heat: the hottest months are March to May; the rainy season runs roughly from May to October.

A real example: two weeks in Cambodia

Daniel and Sophie from Bristol plan two weeks in Cambodia. A week before they fly, they apply for their Cambodia visa on the official e-visa website, upload passport-style photos and pay by card. Both visas arrive by email three days later. They print two copies each and complete the free e-Arrival Card five days before landing in Siem Reap. At the airport they skip the visa-on-arrival queue and go straight to immigration. Their hotel registers them automatically.

How do you extend a Cambodia visa?

If you want to stay longer than 30 days, you can extend a tourist Cambodia visa inside the country before it expires. Many travellers use a licensed travel agent or guesthouse service in Phnom Penh or Siem Reap, which submits the passport to the immigration department. Allow several working days, during which the agent holds your passport, so plan travel around it. Tourist visas allow limited extensions; for long stays, a business visa gives more flexibility.

Cambodia visa for children

Every child needs their own Cambodia visa, applied for with their own passport. If a child travels with only one parent, carry a consent letter from the other parent and a copy of their passport. For a visa on arrival, bring a passport photo for each child.

What should you carry at the border?

  • your passport, valid for six months and undamaged
  • a printed copy of your Cambodia visa, or your e-visa on your phone
  • your e-Arrival Card confirmation if arriving by air
  • proof of your return or onward travel
  • your hotel address

Officers rarely ask for everything, but having it ready keeps the line moving.

When is the best time to visit Cambodia?

The cool, dry season from November to February is the most popular time, with clear skies at Angkor and comfortable temperatures. March to May is very hot. The rainy season, roughly May to October, brings green landscapes, fewer crowds and short heavy showers, usually in the afternoon. Whatever the season, apply for your Cambodia visa at least a week before travel to leave room for any delay.

Is it safe to use a visa agency?

Licensed agencies can help, but many websites only copy the official form and add a large fee. If you use an agency, ask them to show the official government fee separately, confirm they submit through the official system, and never send your original passport by post to an unknown company.

Key takeaways

  • British citizens need a Cambodia visa to visit.
  • Apply for the official e-visa at least four days before travel, or get a visa on arrival in US dollars.
  • A tourist visa allows 30 days from entry and can be extended in Cambodia.
  • Your passport must be valid for six months and undamaged.
  • Complete the free e-Arrival Card if you arrive by air at a main airport.
  • Work needs a business visa and a work permit.

How can Alif Visa help with your Cambodia visa?

Alif Visa is a UK-registered visa assistance company helping travellers worldwide. We can check your e-visa details or prepare your Cambodia visa application, and arrange travel insurance. Check your route or talk to us.

[IMG3]

Frequently asked questions

How long does a Cambodia e-visa take?

Apply at least four days before you travel. Many e-visas arrive sooner, but do not leave it to the last minute.

Can I extend a Cambodia visa?

Yes, a tourist visa can be extended while you are in Cambodia.

Do I need US dollars for a Cambodia visa on arrival?

Yes. The visa on arrival fee is paid in US dollars, so bring the right amount in clean notes.

What is the Cambodia e-Arrival Card?

A free online form you complete within seven days before flying into Phnom Penh, Siem Reap or Sihanoukville.

Can I work in Cambodia on a tourist visa?

No. You need a business visa and a work permit, arranged with your employer.

Is the Angkor Pass included in the Cambodia visa?

No. The Angkor Pass is a separate ticket for the temples.

Can I use my e-visa at any land border?

Not always. Check that your chosen border crossing accepts e-visas before you travel.

Do I need travel insurance for a Cambodia visa?

It is not usually checked for the tourist visa, but medical and evacuation cover is strongly recommended because serious cases may need treatment abroad.

Can I get a Cambodia visa for my whole family in one application?

No. Each traveller, including children, needs their own visa, though you can submit them one after another in the same session.

What is a Belgium visa?

a visa for a short stay is a Schengen visa issued by Belgium. It lets you stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism, family visits or business, and travel to other Schengen countries during that time. You apply to Belgium if it is your main destination, or your first point of entry when all stays are equal in length.

Long stays, such as work, study or family reunion, need a national Belgium visa (type D), which follows a different process.

Do UK residents need a Belgium visa?

It depends on your passport:

  • British citizens do not need a visa for short visits. They will need ETIAS authorisation once the EU starts it.
  • UK residents with other passports, such as Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian, Chinese or Filipino passports, usually need a Schengen visa.
  • Residence permit: your UK residence permit should normally be valid for at least three months after you plan to leave the Schengen area.

Our Schengen visa from the UK guide explains this in more detail.

How do you apply for a Belgium visa, step by step?

Here are seven easy steps to apply for a visa from the UK.

  1. Check you need a visa and that Belgium is your main destination.
  2. Create an account on the TLScontact Belgium (UK) website and fill in the application.
  3. Book an appointment at the centre covering your area: London, Edinburgh or Manchester.
  4. Prepare your documents using the TLScontact checklist.
  5. Attend the appointment, hand in your file and passport, give fingerprints and pay the fees.
  6. Track your application on TLScontact and collect your passport when it is ready.
  7. Declare your presence within three days of arriving in Belgium. From 10 April 2026 this can be done online via "My Address in Belgium".

What documents do you need for a Belgium visa?

The Embassy decides on the file you submit, so send complete documents the first time. A typical Belgium visa file includes:

  • Passport valid for at least three months after your return, with two blank pages, issued in the last 10 years
  • UK residence permit, such as an eVisa share code or residence card, and proof you live in the UK
  • Completed application form and a recent photo (see our photo guide)
  • Travel insurance with at least €30,000 medical cover for the whole Schengen area
  • Flight and hotel bookings, or an invitation from your host in Belgium
  • Recent bank statements and an employment or study letter
  • A short cover letter explaining your trip

How much does a Belgium visa cost?

The Schengen visa fee is set by the EU and is currently €90 for adults, with reduced fees for children aged 6 to 11 and no fee for children under 6. TLScontact adds a service fee, and optional services such as courier return cost extra. The current amounts are shown on the TLScontact website.

[IMG2]

How long does a Belgium visa take?

Schengen consulates aim to decide within 15 calendar days of a complete application. Some cases take longer, up to 45 days, especially in busy seasons. You can apply up to six months before travel. Apply at least three to four weeks ahead to allow time for appointments and possible questions.

What is the 3-day presence declaration?

Anyone entering Belgium for a short stay must declare their presence within three days of arrival. Hotels usually do this for their guests. If you stay with family or friends, you must do it yourself. From 10 April 2026, this can be done online through "My Address in Belgium" (MAB), so you no longer need to go to the town hall.

Belgium visa for family visits

If you visit family in Belgium, your host can send an invitation letter with their contact details and a copy of their Belgian ID card or residence permit. If they will pay for your stay, they can also sign a formal guarantee of support (Annex 3bis) at their town hall. This can replace some of your own proof of funds.

Belgium visa for business trips

For business, add an invitation letter from the Belgian company, a letter from your UK employer confirming your role and approved leave, and proof of who pays for the trip. Brussels hosts the EU institutions and many international organisations, so conference and meeting invitations are common supporting documents.

What about British citizens and ETIAS?

British citizens do not need a visa for short visits. When the EU's ETIAS travel authorisation starts, they will need to apply online before travelling. See our ETIAS guide.

Which Belgium visa mistakes should you avoid?

  • Applying at the embassy instead of TLScontact
  • A UK residence permit that expires too soon after your trip
  • Travel insurance that does not cover the whole Schengen area
  • Bank statements with sudden large deposits
  • Choosing Belgium when another Schengen country is your main destination
  • Forgetting the 3-day presence declaration

A real example: a family visit to Antwerp

Chidi, a Nigerian citizen working as a pharmacist in Manchester, wants to visit his sister in Antwerp for two weeks. He books an appointment at the TLScontact centre in Manchester. His sister sends an invitation letter, a copy of her Belgian residence card and a signed guarantee of support. Chidi adds his UK residence permit, a letter from his employer, six months of payslips and bank statements, travel insurance and his flights. His Belgium visa is approved in ten days. When he arrives, his sister helps him declare his presence online through My Address in Belgium.

Belgium visa vs other Schengen visas

SituationWhich visa to apply for
Your whole trip is in BelgiumBelgium visa
Most days are in Belgium, a short trip to ParisBelgium visa
Equal days in Belgium and the Netherlands, entering via BrusselsBelgium visa
Most days are in FranceFrench Schengen visa

Can you get a multiple-entry Belgium visa?

Yes. If you travel to Belgium or the Schengen area often and have used previous Schengen visas correctly, you may be given a multiple-entry Belgium visa valid for one year or longer. Under the EU's "cascade" rules, regular travellers with a good visa history can receive visas with longer validity. Mention your past visas in your cover letter and include copies.

Short courses and training

A short course of less than 90 days can be done on a short-stay Belgium visa. Include your enrolment letter, proof of fees paid and accommodation. Courses longer than 90 days need a national (type D) Belgium visa for study.

What if your Belgium visa is refused?

The refusal decision explains the reasons. You can appeal to Belgium's Council for Alien Law Litigation within the deadline stated in the decision, usually 30 days, or reapply with a stronger file. Most refusals relate to doubts about the purpose of the trip, proof of money or your intention to return. Address each reason directly in a new application.

Travel insurance for a Belgium visa

Your insurance must:

  • cover at least €30,000 for medical emergencies, hospital treatment and repatriation
  • be valid in all Schengen countries
  • cover the whole period of your stay

Bring the policy certificate, not just a receipt. Our travel insurance service arranges policies that meet these rules.

Belgium visa and the 90/180 rule

a visa counts towards the Schengen 90/180 rule: you can spend at most 90 days in any rolling 180-day period across all Schengen countries. Days on earlier trips count. Before booking, add up the days you have spent in the Schengen area in the last 180 days, so your new trip does not take you over the limit.

What happens at the TLScontact centre?

On the day, arrive on time with your appointment confirmation, passport and documents. Staff check the file, scan your documents, take your fingerprints and photo, and collect the fees. You can buy optional services such as SMS updates or courier return. Keep your receipt; it has the reference number you need to track your visa.

Key takeaways

  • UK residents who need a Schengen visa apply for a visa at TLScontact, not the embassy.
  • Centres are in London, Edinburgh and Manchester; use the one for your area.
  • Bring proof of UK residence, insurance with €30,000 cover, money and travel plans.
  • Most decisions take up to 15 days; apply three to four weeks ahead.
  • Declare your presence within three days of arrival.
  • British citizens do not need a visa for short visits but will need ETIAS once it starts.

Can I apply for a Belgium visa at the embassy in London?

No. Short-stay visa applications go through TLScontact visa application centres, not the embassy.

Which TLScontact centre should I use?

Use the centre that covers where you live: London, Edinburgh or Manchester.

How long can I stay on a Belgium visa?

Up to 90 days in any 180-day period, depending on the dates and entries on your visa.

Do I need to register when I arrive in Belgium?

Yes, visitors must declare their presence within three days. From 10 April 2026 this can be done online through My Address in Belgium. Hotels usually handle it for guests.

Do British citizens need a Belgium visa?

No, not for short visits. They will need ETIAS authorisation once it begins.

The Schengen visa fee is currently €90 for adults, plus the TLScontact service fee.

How long is my UK residence permit required to be valid?

Normally at least three months after you plan to leave the Schengen area.

Can I visit other Schengen countries on a Belgium visa?

Yes, during its validity, as long as Belgium is your main destination and you stay within 90 days in any 180-day period.

Can my family member in Belgium sponsor my Belgium visa?

Yes. They can send an invitation letter and sign a guarantee of support (Annex 3bis) at their town hall, which helps prove your funds.

Do I need an appointment to apply for a Belgium visa in the UK?

Yes. Book online on the TLScontact Belgium (UK) website before you go to the centre. Walk-in applications are not usually accepted.
